request.spec:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

agent.result_text:
I added the policy export button. The "policy export" test now passes, and so do scenarios 1 and 3. **Scenario 2 still fails**, at a step unrelated to the export, so `bin/e2e` does not fully pass yet.

**What I changed** (front end only, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/settings/settings.ts`)
- A new button, `data-testid="export-policy"`, sits next to "Show policy versions". It downloads `policy.csv` with the header `version,from,key,value,claims,due-total`, then one line per version, oldest first.
- **claims** is the number of the sheet's claims that belong to that version. A claim belongs to the latest version whose from-date is on or before the claim's date, which is how the existing "Show policy versions" list counts them.
- **due-total** adds up the due of those claims that count in the live totals: open, pending or settled. It is not capped.
- A version with no from-date leaves the `from` field blank.
- The server and database needed no changes, because the sheet already sends its policy versions to the screen.

**The scenario 2 failure**
- At `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:947` the test expects user "vic" to be refused when soft-closing period 2026-04, but the app allows it.
- It also fails without my change: I took the button out and ran the suite again, and scenario 2 failed at the same line.
- My reading of the cause, which I haven't confirmed: vic has the "restricted" role, and the sheet's permission setting for closing periods is "clerk". The server treats every role other than steward as a clerk when it checks permissions, so a restricted user passes. The test seems to expect a restricted user to be refused when only clerks are listed.
- I didn't change this, because it would change how permissions work for restricted users across the whole app. Tell me if you want me to make that change.

probe.probe_text:
# How the sheet's figures and rules are worked out

The main places are the server's `rollup/Rollup.java` and `sheet/Sheet.java`, the `claim/ClaimService.java` and `person/PersonService.java` method notes, and the front end's `core/figures.ts` and `core/claims.ts`. One thing to know first: **the screen does not show the server's figures.** The server sends raw claims and people, and the front end works out claimed, due, overdue and so on again on its own (`figures.ts` and `claims.ts`). The server works out the same figures in `Rollup` for the audit lines, the totals across child sheets, period closes and statements. I read the main rules in full and skimmed most of the rest through the comments above each method, so treat the less central items as "as documented".

## 1. Figures and the rules behind them

### Per claim

- **amount**: two decimals. While a claim has `lines`, its amount is what the lines add up to. A negative amount is a **correction** (`isCorrection`). It must name, in `corrects`, a SETTLED claim of the same person, and it can't be more than what is left of that claim.
- **date**: defaults to the sheet's `entryDate` while that is set, otherwise the sheet's `today` (`SheetService` "default date").
- **dueBy**: fixed when the claim is added. It is the `termsFor` count of business days after the claim's date, skipping weekends and `Holiday`s. The terms come from the person's own `PersonTerms`, else their grade's `terms-<grade>`, else the sheet's `terms` (14 before any is set). Later changes to the terms don't move it. Adding a holiday works it out again for claims that are not SETTLED or VOID, unless `dueBySet` is on (a steward set it directly).
- **due**, the per-claim figure (`Rollup.figure` / `charged`, mirrored by `figureCents` / `claimDue` in the front end):
  1. `settledDue` if the claim is settled (frozen); otherwise
  2. `statedDue` if a statement bound it (`isBound`); otherwise
  3. the live due: `amount × rate / 100`. The rate is the one `inForce` for the person's grade `gradeOn(claim date)`, looked up on this sheet, then its parent sheets (up to three levels up), then the sheet it was cloned from (`findWithAncestors`). A forward-only rate does not apply to claims that were already on the sheet when it was saved (`Rate.forClaim`). No rate means **n/a**.
  - **Rounding**: `Sheet.rounding(roundingDate)` uses the `rounding` setting in force on that date. With no setting, claims dated before `policyDate` (or the sheet's today when there is none) round HALF_UP, and later ones HALF_EVEN. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
  - Then `charged`: at least `floorOn(date)` (1.00 by default). Then, only for OPEN or PENDING claims that are not `waived`, a **late charge** (`Sheet.lateCharge`): for each full 30 days past `lateFrom`, add the `latePctOn` that 30-day boundary date, applied to the figure plus the charges so far (compounding). Each step is rounded the way the claim's date rounds.
  - `lateFrom` is the due-by plus `grace-<grade>`, taken for the grade in force on the claim's date.
  - Settled, bound and correction claims get no floor and no charge.
- **overdue** (`Rollup.overdue` / `Claims.overdue`): OPEN or PENDING, not `deferredOn(today)`, and `lateFrom` is before the sheet's today.
- **deferred** (`deferredOn`): the claim's status counts, no statement binds it, and today is before `deferredUntil`. While deferred it counts in no total, is not overdue and cannot be settled.
- **Parts (shares)**: other people can each hold a percentage of a claim, up to 100.00 in total (`ClaimShare`).
  - A holder's part is `amount × share × the holder's own grade rate / 10⁴`, rounded the way the claim rounds (`Rollup.part`).
  - If the claim is settled, the part is `settledDue × share / 100`, rounded HALF_EVEN (`ClaimShare.part`).
  - The claim's own person counts the figure less all the parts.
- **Flags and other fields on a claim**: `waived`, `held`, `lateEntry` (added while its period was soft-closed), `remindedOn` and `escalated`, `lockedBy`, `settleBatch`, `splitFrom`, the proofs counts, `reviewAssignee`, `voidReason`, the status log, and `number`.
  - A claim gets its `number` when it is settled. It comes from `nextClaimNumber`: per fiscal year, or per period while `numbersByPeriod` is on.
  - "Late for review" and "pending late" come from `reviewSla` and `pendingSla`.

### Statuses and transitions (`ClaimStatus`)

- A claim goes DRAFT → OPEN, or to REVIEW instead of OPEN when its due is above `reviewThresholdOn`. A steward's review moves REVIEW → OPEN.
- Settling moves OPEN → SETTLED, or to PENDING instead when a clerk settles a due above `clerkLimitFor`. PENDING then goes to SETTLED by approval or back to OPEN by rejection.
- VOID can be reached from any of these. DELETED only from DRAFT; it can be restored to DRAFT only on the same sheet today it was deleted.
- `counts()` is true for OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED. `isOpen()` is true for OPEN and PENDING.

### Per person (`Rollup.Figures`, mirrored in `Figures`)

- **Which claims count** (`countsClaimed` / `live()`): the status counts, the claim is not deferred, and it is not `retiredOut`. A claim is retiredOut when it is OPEN or PENDING, unbound, and the person's retirement date has been reached on the sheet's today.
- **claimed**: the amounts of counting claims, leaving out corrections.
- **dueTotal**: the person's own share of each counting claim's figure, plus the parts they hold of other people's claims.
  - It is **n/a (null)** unless their grade on today has a rate, or at least one claim keeps a figure.
  - Then it is `capped`: at most `capOn(the date of their latest counting claim, or today if none)` minus their **cutTotal**, and that limit is never below 0.00.
- **overdueTotal**: the full figure of each overdue claim (not reduced by parts). **overdueCount** counts overdue claims even when they have no figure.
- **settledTotal / openTotal**: the person's share of SETTLED claims, and of OPEN plus PENDING claims, with corrections included.
- **score**: (the full figures of their SETTLED claims that aren't corrections, minus 500 × overdueCount) / 100, rounded HALF_EVEN to a whole number.
  - The **band** (front end only) is HIGH or MID against the high and mid score thresholds. It shows only while both are set.
- **cutTotal** (`PoolController.cutTotals`): `cuts` gives each pool member a share of the pot, `pot × share / sum of shares`, rounded HALF_EVEN, and the rounding remainder goes to the smallest non-zero cut.
  - Retired members, members on hold, and members not active on today get nothing, and their share is spread over the others.
  - A nested pool's pot is its cut in the pool above it. Crews are equal-share pools.
- **Front-end-only figures**:
  - `excessCents`: how far the sum is above the cap.
  - aged buckets: 0–30, 31–60 and 61+ days.
  - "active": an open counting claim within the last 30 days.
  - the 90-day settled figure.
  - tag and month totals, crew and watched totals, the steward dashboard, and the rate what-if preview.
- **Statements**: `statementCount`, `statedTotal` and `statementDate`.
  - Taking a statement records the person's due-total and binds each counting claim to its current shown due, late charge and floor included.
  - Cancelling one (steward only) unbinds those claims.

### Sheet totals

- **claimedTotal**: a plain sum.
- **dueTotal / overdueTotal**: `trimmed`, meaning the sum less the single highest and the single lowest value when there are three or more people. n/a due-totals are skipped.
- **Grade breakdown**: due by the grade in force on today, leaving out retired people. Claims are also counted by status.
- **Totals across child sheets**: `descendants` adds up each child sheet's own trimmed totals.

### Periods (`Period`, plus `Rollup.dueBetweenByPerson`, `carriedByPerson` and `openByPerson`)

- A claim belongs to the period that contains its due-by.
- **Period due**: counts by the status the claim had at the end of the period's last day, from its status log.
- **Carried**: claims from earlier periods that were still open at this period's end, plus the person's opening balance.
- **Close and soft-close** both freeze the due-total, each person's due and carried figures, and the pool cuts.
  - A closed period refuses every change to its claims (`refuseClosed`). A soft-closed one still allows changes, and claims added then are flagged `lateEntry`.
  - Reopening is allowed for stewards by the standing rule, and is blocked while the period is `locked`.
  - Moving the sheet's today forward closes open periods once their end date plus the sheet's grace days has passed (a sheet setting; "grace days" also names a per-grade setting).
  - The year-end rollover, which only a steward can run, adds each person's open figure to the next year's opening balance and soft-closes the old year's periods.
- **Caps on open claims**: a period can cap how many OPEN or PENDING claims a person may have in it, and the sheet can set a `maxOpen` per person.

### Who may do what

- **Roles**: clerk (the default for any name), steward, viewer, or restricted (sees only themselves and their crews). A steward can delegate the steward role for a range of the sheet's days; audit lines then end `for=<steward>`.
- **`STANDING_PERMISSIONS`**: open, settle, void, close and change-today are allowed to clerks and stewards; reassign and reopen to stewards. The permission matrix overrides these.
- **Steward only**: review, approve, reject, waive, re-settle, re-date, set due-by, cancel a statement, merge, transfer, flag, rollover, archive, and voiding a settled claim (only within 7 days of settling).
  - The person's named `approver` may also approve and reject their claims.
- **Four-eyes rule**: the user who opened or last edited a claim can't settle or approve it.
- **Opening is refused** for a flagged person (unless by a steward), with an empty note when the due is above the note threshold, over the period cap, or over `maxOpen`.
- **Settling or approving needs proof** when the due is above `proofThresholdFor`; with proof kinds set, at least one of each kind.
- **Refused for everyone**:
  - every change on a viewer's or an archived sheet's screen, and any change from an as-of view;
  - a claim dated after the person's retirement;
  - editing a claim whose editor another user has open (`lockedBy`).

### Holds, imports and the sheet's today

- **Person hold**: only takes the person's cut out of the pools (`Rollup.heldOut` says so explicitly). **Claim hold** (`held`): a toggle that is audited and shown, but no figure reads it.
- **Imports**: imports of people, rates and opening balances, and pasting claims, are all-or-nothing; any refused line refuses the whole import.
  - Import updates people who match by name or alias, and adds the rest. A blank grade becomes `defaultGradeOrA`.
  - A pasted line that matches an existing DRAFT updates it and then opens it.
- **Changing the sheet's today** writes SNAPSHOT lines (plus SCORE lines while the score log is on), releases every editor lock, and closes periods past their grace days.
- Settling or approving as of an earlier date freezes the due as it stood then.

## 2. How hard it was to follow

It is hard to follow, and there is no one place a new developer could pick it up. Each figure is worked out at least twice: `Rollup.java` on the server and `figures.ts`/`claims.ts` in the front end, with part of it repeated a third time in `ClaimService` (`liveDue`/`shownDue`). Inside `Rollup` the same settled → bound → live chain is copied four times, and the rules are scattered across entity, controller (`PoolController.cutTotals`) and service classes.

The comments don't always match the code:
- **Holds**: `Person`, `Claim.held`, the statement method and front-end notes say a hold leaves claims out of the totals, but `Rollup.heldOut` checks retirement only.
- **Clerk limit**: it uses the person's grade on the sheet's today, while every other figure uses the grade on the claim's date.

Taken together, the code that actually runs, not its comments, is the only reliable guide.
